answers.text: Tell the AI: from the driver's message, always give exactly three lines in this order - drop-off time, pallet count, any damage noted - using those exact labels each time.
Turn the week's call log into a list with time, customer, topic, outcome, and count up how many need a follow-up call at the end.
The timing in that note seems a bit tight to me but I'm not sure exactly what's wrong with it.
I checked the on-time rate, 9 late out of 118, and that's about 92%, matching what they wrote. But the increase from 96 to 118 invoices looks more like 23% to me, not the 20% stated.
I'd go with Output 2, since it shows the actual ticket numbers behind the 88%. Output 1 is just the percentage with nothing backing it up.
I'd probably send the second one since it has more detail in it.

I'd say no to the home address at least - that's someone's personal details, not something to put through a tool we haven't checked. Not sure about the rest of it, so I'd probably just hold the whole lot back to be safe.
I'd hold back the hourly rates and retainer cap before pasting anything in.
I'd just double check the numbers look right before sending it on.
I think the first step, where the AI reads the invoice PDF and pulls out the line items, is the one that could cause problems if it gets it wrong.
